findings.issue: Several docs still reference canonical files that do not yet exist as standalone canonical docs (e.g. EVENT_BUS.md, ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES.md, FAILURE_MODEL.md links are used as anchoring references but the audit should verify they are truly canonical in the repo).
Terms are not yet centralized in a single glossary; canonicals are dispersed across multiple specs, increasing synonym risk (e.g. Mission Engine / Mission Engine runtime / Orchestrator boundaries).
Planner, Orchestrator, Mission Engine, and Coordinator are not yet strictly disambiguated in a single ownership matrix.
Some state machines define additional transitions in prose but not in explicit forbidden-transition tables.
Event publisher/consumer ownership is implied but not fully enumerated for every event type.
Security model is present in pieces, but secrets handling and encryption boundaries are not fully centralized in one interface-level spec.
Schemas have schema_version, but protocols and higher-order docs do not yet uniformly define migration_strategy and compatibility fields in a machine-readable way.
Requirements-to-test traceability is not yet represented as a formal matrix or artifact.

recommendations: Add a canonical glossary/spec index with single-source definitions for all core terms.
Add an ownership matrix mapping every stateful artifact to exactly one writer and one reader tier.
Normalize versioning metadata across schemas and protocols: schema_version, protocol_version, compatibility, migration_strategy.
Create a machine-readable traceability matrix from requirement -> spec -> protocol -> implementation package -> test.
Introduce a dedicated security model spec for secrets, auth, sandboxing, encryption, and audit boundaries.

phase_0_7_recommendation.name: Specification Lock
criteria: Assign semantic versions to every frozen spec (v1.0.0).
Maintain changelog entries for every spec change.
Require an ADR for any frozen-spec modification.
